narrative.title: Re-sequencing the Badge Scanners by Turn Parity
narrative.scenario: A security line records badge scans in order, and the auditor wants all odd-numbered turns processed first followed by all even-numbered turns — positions keep their relative order within each group, and the value on each badge never changes. The controllers rewrite the links in place, threading two sub-sequences and then joining the tail of the first to the head of the second.
narrative.inputFormat: An array head of node values representing the linked list.
narrative.outputFormat: The values after regrouping: nodes from 1-based odd positions first, then even positions, relative order preserved within each group.

testCases.explanation: Odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th) lead in order, then the even ones follow.

hintLevels: Level 1: Parity of position decides the destination — values never change, only the order of the chain does.
Level 2: Hold the head of the even sub-chain aside, advance an odd tracker and an even tracker in lockstep rewiring every other link, then attach the odd tail to the saved even head.
Level 3: The lockstep advance is the fragile part — the even tracker must move only after the odd rewire lands, or a short list will send a tracker through null.
